artists.biography:
Om is an American stoner rock and drone metal band from San Francisco, formed in 2003 by bassist and vocalist Al Cisneros and drummer Chris Hakius, both formerly of the influential sludge/stoner band Sleep. The group emerged with a stripped-down duo format that emphasized heavy repetition, hypnotic grooves, and droning bass lines, drawing on spiritual, mystical, and Eastern religious imagery. Their name references the Hindu sacred syllable “Om,” reflecting the band’s meditative and transcendental approach to heavy music.

Om’s early releases, beginning with Variations on a Theme and continuing through albums such as Pilgrimage and Conference of the Birds, established their signature blend of minimalism, doom-laden riffing, and chant-like intensity. After Hakius’s departure, the band evolved into a trio with drummer Emil Amos and later added Tyler Trotter on keyboards, broadening their sound while keeping its ritualistic core intact. Albums like God Is Good and Advaitic Songs further expanded their use of Middle Eastern, Byzantine, and drone textures, while live recordings and singles such as “Gebel Barkal” reinforced their reputation for immersive, spiritual heaviness.

Widely respected in underground rock and metal circles, Om helped define a more contemplative, expansive branch of stoner and doom metal. Their music stands out for transforming volume and repetition into something almost devotional, influencing a wide range of heavy and experimental artists.

perplexity.description:
Pilgrimage is the third studio album by American drone metal band Om and their first release for Southern Lord, arriving at a pivotal moment in the group’s evolution. Recorded at Electrical Audio with Steve Albini, the album captures the stripped-down power that would define Om’s early work: massive bass lines, disciplined drumming, and a hypnotic, mantra-like focus that turns repetition into momentum. It is also the final Om studio album to feature drummer Chris Hakius, giving the record added significance within the band’s catalog.

Across its four extended tracks — including the title piece, “Unitive Knowledge of the Godhead,” and “Bhima’s Theme” — Pilgrimage balances heaviness with a meditative, כמעט ritualistic atmosphere. The result is one of Om’s most celebrated releases, often regarded as a key statement of their sound: austere, immersive, and spiritually charged, yet anchored by a tight, physical groove. Its reception has remained strong enough to keep it in demand, underscoring its status as a defining album in modern heavy music.
